Two retrieval fixes for prose, plus the benchmark kit that measures them. Supersedes #100, #103
and #101, which are closed in favour of this.

Code is `internal/sem` only (438 insertions); everything else is `bench/memory/` — docs, adapters
and patch files. No Go outside the prose path is touched.

---

## The defect

`selectSearchCandidates` admits **one candidate per file**. For code that is right — a file is
the thing you open. For prose it is wrong: a markdown document's heading regions already exist in
the graph as `section` entities (`parser.go` `markdownEntities`), are already scored, and are then
collapsed to one per file.

Measured on a real prose corpus at `--top-k 200`, the shipped build returned **19 results across
19 files while carrying 195 passages holding 42 KB of evidence** that no `results[]` consumer
could reach. Ranks 6–19 got a one-line snippet.

**Commit 1 — multi-resolution prose retrieval.** When fewer distinct files match than `--top-k`
asked for, spend the spare slots promoting those regions to results of their own. Strictly
additive: runs after selection, only fills slots the distinct-file ranking left empty, never
breaches `--max-context-bytes`. `--single-resolution` restores the old output.

That alone was not enough, because promoted regions are **satellites**: `Score: parent.Score`
verbatim, ordered by a round-robin over *parent index*, appended after every parent. Result:

```
200 results  ->  19 distinct scores
```

181 of 200 are score-duplicates of one of 19 parents. A consumer sorting by score with a stable
sort therefore gets 19 blocks — one document's parent followed by its regions, then the next.
Truncate to the top 50/20/10 and you see only the first one or two documents. Evidence that must
be stitched across documents structurally cannot surface.

**Commit 2 — rank prose sections as independent candidates.** The retrieval unit becomes the
section (`proseParentKey`, keyed by the heading's SymbolID, falling back to file path where a
document has no section structure). A section competes on its own score, as an independent file
would. Breadth is preserved: **no document gets a second region until every document that fits
has one**, binding every selection pass. `--document-resolution` restores the previous behaviour.

Both changes are query-blind. The unit comes from the parser's section entities and the file
extension; nothing reads the question.

## Measured — 152 questions, real prose corpus, identical search arguments

| | items/q | distinct regions/q | **distinct scores/q** | files/q | visible chars/q |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 195.0 | 243.0 | **17.1** | 18.9 | 60,854 |
| **after** | **196.0** | **295.3** | **84.9** | **18.9** | **53,929** |
| off switch | 195.0 | 243.0 | 17.1 | 18.9 | 60,854 |

Score diversity 17.1 → 84.9, document coverage unchanged, and **11.4% fewer bytes** — the old
build computed regions and discarded them unread. The off switch is byte-identical to the
previous behaviour on every metric.

## Code search is unaffected

**30 of 30 full-JSON payloads identical** — 15 real locate queries against this repo at
`--top-k 10` *and* `--top-k 50`, comparing entire payloads (results element by element plus
`stats`, `commit`, `tree`, `completeness`, `diagnostics`), latency telemetry excluded.

The prose branch sits behind `proseParentCorpus`, requiring ≥4 units and ≥80% doc-extension
paths — a source repo cannot reach it. Verified rather than asserted: three deliberately
documentation-flavoured queries against this Go repo returned **zero** results carrying
`retrieval_mode=prose-parent` in either build.

## Benchmark result

LoCoMo, all 1540 questions, answerer **and** judge both `gpt-5.6-sol`, `top_k=200`, against a
mem0 OSS control **running concurrently in the same window**. No harness flag, no ingest change —
the shipped corpus shape.

| | overall | single-hop | multi-hop | temporal | open-domain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **entire-graph** | **94.74** | **96.67** | **93.97** | **95.33** | 78.12 |
| mem0 OSS | 93.83 | 95.12 | 93.62 | 94.70 | **80.21** |

**+0.91pp overall, discordant 43–29, McNemar p = 0.125 — statistically tied, point estimate
favours entire-graph.** That wording follows a decision rule registered before the run finished.
**single-hop +1.55pp, p = 0.035** is the one cell significant on its own.

Multi-hop moved from **−1.44 against mem0 to +0.35** — the deficit this change targets, and the
category the 19-distinct-scores collapse was starving.

The isolated effect of commit 1, measured paired on the same corpus with the binary as the only
variable: **91.56 → 93.83, +2.27pp, discordant 46–11, p = 3.3e-06, n = 1540.**

### Stated plainly

- Run-to-run noise on this harness is **0.65pp** — two identical mem0 runs scored 93.83 and 93.57.
- entire-graph delivers ~30% more context per question, and **mem0 is more context-efficient
  below ~25k chars** (43.2 accuracy points per 1k chars at top-10 against our 5.7). `top_k`
  equalises item count, not context volume.
- Prose search is **2.1× slower per query** (0.300s → 0.628s); passages are planned for ~196
  units instead of 19. Code-search latency is unchanged.
- Open-domain is our one losing category.

## The benchmark kit

`bench/memory/` makes every number above reproducible: the entire-graph adapter, the competitor
ports we wrote, the fairness spec, a run index, and apply-checked patches for the four upstream
files we modified. Upstream is pinned by **md5-verified fork point**, not a guessed SHA, and the
judge/answerer prompts are byte-identical to upstream — we did not tune the grading.

**Three competitor defects were found and fixed in the competitors' favour**: mem0 **+6.04**
(a `limit` kwarg silently capping search at 20 memories instead of 200), cognee **+13.77**
(state on disk with an in-memory retrieval buffer, so resumed runs searched nothing), and cmm
from **structurally zero** (its shipped BM25 excludes `Section` nodes, so prose returns no
results). A fourth, against mem0, is disclosed rather than fixed — it is measured at 0.13pp.

## Tests

`mise run check` green. Three regressions were found and fixed during development, each pinned by
a test: whole-document exclusion at small top-k, loss of same-document passages at tight top-k,
and one region returned up to seven times.

## Review of the new changes to PR #104

Since our last review, one commit landed: `7ef28b9 fix(search): keep section units off code, keep results score-ordered`, responding to the seven findings from that review. **Verdict: all seven are genuinely addressed, tests are green, and I independently confirmed the code-search parity claim. One residual gap in the containment fix is worth a follow-up, though I could not reproduce it.**

Note on where the review history lived: my persistent memory had no PR 104 entry — the prior reviews were in the Entire checkpoint history (round 1 on the benchmark kit, Aug 15; round 2 with the seven code findings). I've now saved the review state to memory so next time it's actually there.

### Verification of the seven fixes

1. **Section units leaking into code results** — fixed correctly. `proseParentKey` and the `planProseParentPassages` call in `selectSearchCandidates` are both gated on `proseParentPath(...)` (doc extension check), so a code file in a docs-heavy repo falls back to file-keyed units and never gets passage plans. This closes both leak routes: section keying uncapping `MaxRegionsPerFile`, and promotion handing code files extra slots (`internal/sem/search_prose_parent.go:45-63`, `:152-159`).
2. **Score ordering** — fixed. `applyProseResolutionPromotions` now stable-sorts descending by score and renumbers ranks; since parents enter in descending order and promotions tie their parents exactly, membership is unchanged and the array is monotone again. Pinned by `TestExpandProseResolutionKeepsResultsScoreOrdered`.
3. **Contained duplicates** — fixed for ranked results. `dropContainedProseResults` runs after snippet growth and before promotion, drops only prose results, and is a provable no-op under the off-switches (document resolution means one result per file, so same-file containment can't occur — the byte-identical claim for the off switch holds).
4. **Fitter O(n) serialization** — the bisection is sound. I checked `applyProseResolutionPromotions` for purity (fresh slices throughout, safe to call repeatedly) and the monotonicity assumption holds: each promotion moves a passage into a strictly larger full result record. Edge cases (nothing fits → `low == 0`, zero budget → apply all) match the old loop's behavior.
5. **`SingleResolution` doc comment** and 7. **help text** — both corrected accurately; the new text matches actual behavior (the flags stack, and restoring the old payload needs both).
6. **Scale guard on the default path** — real coverage now: the new fixture builds 20 sections per file so section keys actually differ from file keys, with a linearity assertion, a breadth assertion (20 results across 20 documents), and a benchmark.

### Independent verification

- `go test ./internal/sem/` at `7ef28b9`: **passes** (61s).
- Built the pre-fix (`4f88580`) and post-fix binaries and diffed full JSON search payloads on this repo across 3 queries × top-k 10/50, including deliberately docs-flavored queries: **all six identical** (latency fields excluded). The commit's parity claim checks out. (My first comparison pass was vacuous due to a wrong CLI invocation producing empty output — the rerun above is the valid one.)

### One residual finding (plausible, not reproduced)

The containment fix covers ranked **results** but not promoted **passages** across parents. Sequence: `allocateSearchSnippets` grows windows → `allocateProseParentPassages` attaches passages, overlap-checked against **their own parent's** grown primary only → `dropContainedProseResults` filters results → `expandProseResolution` promotes passages with no further span check. So a passage planned for section B (say line 100 of a doc) that sits at line 30 — inside section A's grown 80-line head window on the same file — can be promoted and reprint text the payload already shows. This is the same fault class as finding 3, through the promotion route. I built a synthetic prose corpus to trigger it and couldn't (needs same-file multi-section results plus spare slots plus specific window geometry), so it's an edge case, not a blocker. The cheap fix is one more containment filter over planned promotions against printed same-file spans, either in `expandProseResolution` or by re-running the containment check on promoted entries. A related minor trade: a section dropped for containment takes its unpromoted passages with it rather than reassigning them — arguably fine, but worth a conscious decision.

One nit: the sort comment in `search_multi_resolution.go` says a promotion "settles immediately after that parent" — with several parents sharing a score it settles after *all* tied parents. Harmless, comment-only.

My recommendation: this commit resolves round 2; the PR is in good shape to proceed, with the promoted-passage containment gap noted for either a small follow-up commit on this branch or a tracked follow-up issue.
